1.explanation:
1. gather/computed/critical-request-chains-test.js covers the core logic that builds CRCs, where iframe requests currently count as ‘critical’.  
2. audits/critical-request-chains-test.js defines the audit metadata and ensures the computed chains feed into Lighthouse’s audit system.  
3. report/v2/renderer/crc-details-renderer-test.js shows how CRCs render in the report UI, including tree filtering and display of data URIs.  
4. gather/computed/page-dependency-graph-test.js supplies the dependency graph underpinning CRCs; any iframe-exclusion logic must integrate here so the chains omit those nodes.  
5. lib/dependency-graph/node-test.js tests the node abstraction used by the dependency graph, useful when distinguishing request types (e.g. frame vs. document vs. data URI).  
6. gather/computed/trace-of-tab-test.js provides the trace events and networkRecords data passed into page-dependency-graph and CRC computation, so reproducing the iframe and data-URI cases requires accurate trace inputs.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show Lighthouse’s Critical Request Chains (CRC) view treating iframes (e.g. a YouTube embed at “/embed/NZeIrwd_iRs”) and data-URI requests as “critical” even though iframes aren’t render-blocking and data URIs aren’t network requests. In the first image, a YouTube iframe plus its CSS and JS children appear in the CRC tree under the host “paulirish.com”. In the second, a base64 font-woff data URI is listed as a separate critical chain leaf. The goal is to exclude <iframe> network requests (and their descendants) from CRC computation, and to drop or ignore pure data URI requests when building the tree.
